Fantastic service and lovely vets

I want to commend Blacks as a total service but today I want to especially say that Natalie went above and beyond.
I have an 11 week kitten called Nyx. We rescued her from being abandoned as a black cat recently. Today she had new onset diarrhea, vomiting and lethargy and she was getting worse quickly. Natalie triaged her quickly, had a conversation with clinical teams at her practice and at the hospital. We initially booked an appointment out of hours at the hospital but Nyx was just getting worse by the hour and a second call the Quinton branch brought her in as an emergency.
Not only did Nyx get five star care from the vet team, who picked up her issue and gave medication to help right away, we watched Natalie manage the clinic, ring patients, deal with someone who was not being  very understanding on the phone and remained so professional, kind and thoughtful throughout the call.
I'm sorry that we caused the clinic to run out of sorts but how lucky the clinic is to have staff like Natalie, who remained an asset to the brand even when under pressure.
I know Nyx will be under the best care at Blacks, and we are also transfering our other animals to the practice because of the high quality service we have had both routine and emergency care. Thank you so much to the entire team who took what could have been a very scary day and turned it into a positive experience, especially Natalie
Staff very helpful. Vet and nurses kind and understanding. Receptionist helpful

We've been using Blacks Vets in Quinton since getting a puppy in early 2023. I can recommend the practice. The women in reception are friendly and helpful, and we've had positive experiences with the vets and nurses, too. Our dog is very expressive, and they all seem to take it in stride. The prices for routine appointments seem reasonable.

I am extremely disappointed with the advice and lack of care we received from this vet and feel other pet owners should be aware of our experience. My cat Lily gave birth to her first kitten at 4am on Sunday 16th August. By the time I contacted this practice she had gone around 32 hours without delivering another kitten despite us believing there were still kittens inside her. I explained exactly what was happening and that I was worried about such a prolonged gap between kittens. Instead of offering to examine her urgently my concerns were dismissed because Lily was behaving normally and wasn’t visibly distressed. I was told the earliest appointment they could offer was the following afternoon. I wasn’t calling because my cat looked I’ll I was calling because I was concerned about the kittens still inside her and the long break in labour, a cat can only safely pause her labour for 36 hours after this comes a massive risk any vet should know this. Sadly Lily eventually resumed active labour 43 hours after delivering her first kitten at 12.30am and delivered another fully developed kitten who was completely unresponsive. Lily immediately cleaned and stimulated the baby and we also attempted stimulation but there was no breathing, movement or response. The kitten had sadly passed away. When I called this vet the kitten was still actively moving in her belly had they of seen my cat and taken this seriously the kitten would’ve still been alive but instead I now have a grieving mom cat and we are now grieving a tiny kitten we were expecting to welcome into our family and arranging an individual cremation while also dealing with the worry and stress of everything Lily has been through. I have made a formal complaint and have asked the practice to investigate how our call was triaged whether a veterinary surgeon was consulted, why an examination wasn’t offered and why we weren’t advised to seek urgent assessment elsewhere if they couldn’t accommodate us. I would strongly encourage anyone whose pet is pregnant or experiencing complications during labour to advocate for them and seek another veterinary opinion if you don’t feel your concerns are being taken seriously. I sincerely hope this practice reviews what happened and its maternity/emergency triage procedures so another family doesn’t have the experience we’ve had to

I am extremely disappointed by the lack of compassion shown by this practice.
A friend found a stray cat in an appalling condition with a serious eye injury and obvious signs that it urgently needed veterinary care. When she contacted this practice for help, she was told they would only see the cat if she registered it as her own and agreed to pay for treatment. The member of staff was also rude and dismissive throughout the conversation.
Thankfully another veterinary practice stepped in and provided the urgent care the cat desperately needed.
I understand that veterinary practices have costs and cannot provide unlimited free treatment, but I expected concern for an animal that was clearly suffering and respectful advice for someone trying to do the right thing. Instead, we were met with indifference and a complete lack of empathy. They have duty of care and should not turn down animal in need! Seams like its all about money to them. Money making machine and no care about suffering animal.
This experience has seriously damaged my confidence in this practice. They are a disgrace
The best veterinary practice I have ever experienced. True care and dedication to my pets and me over the years.

I have had my cat registered here for about a year now and they have been the best I have ever dealt with. Very gentle with him and they are patient; very clear in what he could have and what the next steps could be. He recently got seen by Emma Griffin and she was a gem, we were quite a late appointment and she was the best. We recommend.

The vet called me today and said that before my dog's next visit, he needs a blood test for Brucella canis (my dog ​​was adopted from Romania). We've had our dog for six years, and I don't see the need for the test, which is required when a dog comes from Romania to the UK. This test was introduced in 2025 and is required to obtain a permit for transport to the UK. I feel the vet was trying to extort money from us because there's no need to do this test when the dog has already been in the UK for so long.

5 stars ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

I can’t thank the team at Blacks enough for the care they gave our beloved kitten- JellyBean. From the moment we arrived, Anisha at reception made us feel so welcome and reassured. Her kindness and calm manner really helped ease our nerves during a stressful time.

The lead vet (a lovely gentleman whose name I sadly cannot remember) was absolutely brilliant. He was incredibly gentle and patient with JellyBean, who hasn’t been feeling her best. His swift diagnosis and clear explanation of the treatment plan gave us so much confidence, and we were able to start medication right away.

Both Anisha and the vet showed genuine compassion—not just for JellyBean, but for us as worried pet parents. It’s rare to find such a combination of professionalism and heartfelt care. We’re so grateful.

Highly recommend this practice to anyone who wants their furry family members treated with the utmost love and respect.
